data.intro: Message played when the menu opens

data_description.provider_ips: Comma separated. Empty disables filtering. Behind a proxy you also need use_x_forwarded_for and trusted_proxies.
data_description.allowed_phones: Comma separated. Leave empty to allow every caller.
data_description.technoline_api_key: Required for voice alerts. You must also ask their technical team to approve your server's outbound IP address.
data_description.technoline_announce_extension: The extension the alert call is connected to. Leave empty for automatic discovery, which works when the account has exactly one streaming extension.
data_description.technoline_announce_hours: Automatically hold calls between 23:00 and 08:00. Off by default — a home alert blocked at night misses exactly what it exists for.
data_description.yemot_token: Needed only for the voice alert service. The menu itself does not use it.
data_description.sip_server: The address the provider gave for the line, for example sip.example.com.
data_description.sip_port: 5060 unless the provider says otherwise. UDP only.
data_description.intro: What the caller hears first, before the list of keys. Optional.
data_description.sip_username: The line's username at the provider. Usually a number.
data_description.pbx_alert_url: The address of the alert service installed on the PBX, for example http://192.168.1.5:5000/ha. Needed only for alert calls.
data_description.pbx_trunk: The trunk the PBX dials alerts through.
data_description.pbx_alert_secret: The secret set when the alert service was installed on the PBX.
data_description.pbx_audiosocket_host: The address Home Assistant listens on for the PBX, for the voice assistant. 0.0.0.0 when the PBX is on another machine.
data_description.pbx_audiosocket_port: 9010 unless changed in the PBX dialplan.

send_call.name: Voice alert
send_call.description: Calls the recipients and plays a message. The speech is generated in Home Assistant using the voice of the pipeline you selected. Use this service when the recipients change from alert to alert; for a fixed list you can also use assist_satellite.announce, which has no recipients field and always calls the numbers configured in the integration.

message.name: Message
message.description: The text that is read out on the call.

phones.name: Phone numbers
phones.description: A single number, or several separated by commas. Each recipient gets its own call. Empty calls the numbers configured in the integration.

trunk.name: Outbound trunk
trunk.description: Not every provider supports this: the trunk to dial out on, for a different caller ID. Empty uses the entry's default trunk.

config_entry_id.name: Provider
config_entry_id.description: Which provider entry places the call.

caller_id.name: Caller ID
caller_id.description: The caller ID for the call. Not every provider supports this, and the ID must be approved by the provider — verify it works with them. Empty uses the caller ID the provider or trunk provides.

retries.name: Retries
retries.description: Not every provider supports this: how many times to call back if nobody answers, a minute apart. 0 rings once only.

missing_trunk.title: A trunk missing from the PBX
missing_trunk.description:
Alerts through {missing} will fail: the PBX does not know this trunk. Existing trunks: {available}.

Choose an existing trunk in the integration settings (outbound trunk for alerts) or in the recipient.

sip_auth_failed.title: The SIP line rejected the login
sip_auth_failed.description:
The server {server} rejected the username or password, so calls are not answered and alerts are not sent.

Correct them in the integration settings (line settings).

sip_unreachable.title: The SIP line is not connected
sip_unreachable.description:
The server {server} is not answering, so calls are not answered and alerts are not sent. Home Assistant keeps trying, and this message clears by itself once the line is back.

If it persists, check the server address and port in the integration settings (line settings).
